title: Cover every PC brand and fall back to the motherboard vendor
head: feat/complete-brand-catalogue
body:
## What this changes

The manufacturer mapping was a 23-branch `if` chain, and **DIY / whitebox / re-badged systems matched nothing** because Windows reports `System manufacturer`, `To Be Filled By O.E.M.`, `Default string`, `Unknown`, `OEM` or an empty string for them. Several boutique builders ship exactly those strings.

- **44-entry data table** replacing the chain, covering every brand requested: HP, Dell/Alienware, Lenovo, Acer, ASUS, MSI, Apple, Microsoft Surface, Samsung, Razer, Fujitsu, Dynabook/Toshiba, Framework, LG, HUAWEI, HONOR, Xiaomi/Redmi, Panasonic, VAIO/Sony, MEDION, GIGABYTE, ASRock, Intel, Supermicro, Biostar, ECS, System76, TUXEDO, CHUWI, Teclast, Infinix, itel, Walton, Positivo, Lanix, iBUYPOWER, CyberPowerPC, Falcon Northwest, MAINGEAR, ORIGIN PC, Puget Systems, NZXT, Raspberry Pi, PINE64.
- **Motherboard fallback**: placeholder manufacturers now resolve through the board vendor (`Win32_BaseBoard`, `/sys/class/dmi/id/board_vendor`) and the profile explains that the match came from the board. A real OEM always wins over the board.
- **Honest limits encoded, not hidden**: Apple silicon = VM-only Windows context; Raspberry Pi / PINE64 = ARM boards Windows 10/11 does not run natively; brands without a single global portal return no support URL.
- **Docs**: `docs/vendor-support.md` now lists the catalogue, the fallback and the family precedence rule.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check` clean, `test:source`, `test:security:source`, `test:startup`, `test:release` pass.
- The pure matching code was extracted and executed with `rustc` on this machine: **44 profiles, 0 failures**, including the invariant sweep that caught a `sLC` casing typo.
- New Rust tests: brand coverage (44), placeholder fallback, OEM-over-board precedence, ARM labelling, unknown-vendor behaviour, placeholder normalisation, catalogue invariants. They run in the Windows and Linux CI jobs on this PR.
